objective: Choose a machine, launch an installed CLI, and inspect its session or files in a neutral Material-style workbench.

intake.request: Finally fix the UI please It looks so cluttery and bad No gradient no bluisn colors pills etc use your unparalleled-ui and impeccable skills to enhance the UI and the design so that It feels professional dev tool. Light and Dark, A RAIN ACII Wordmark and LOGO same for the UI as well! I want an google material UI like screen and the typography, spacings etc

state.milestone: Neutral workbench built and inspected; review fixes resolved
state.next_action: Commit reviewed source and design documentation

facts.claim: The owner explicitly requests light/dark, ASCII RAIN identity, Material-like spacing, and bans gradients, bluish colors, and pills.
facts.source: User UI request in this conversation

facts.claim: RAIN has working local/SSH discovery, CLI launching, machine-scoped file editing, terminal controls, and group messaging.
facts.source: apps/rain-client/src/App.tsx and components; seven passing focused tests

facts.claim: Selecting a wrong machine or file path changes where execution and writes occur.

premise.statement: The selected machine anchors launch and file tasks; sessions stay independent of groups. The chrome uses one ASCII identity while task controls remain familiar.
premise.swap_test: Machine context, executable discovery, independent sessions, SSH paths, and group lifecycle are specific to RAIN; replacing the name does not replace those workflows.
invalidated_by: Machine scope disappears during a task
Any blue accent, gradient, or pill returns
Agent sessions terminate when a group is deleted
premise.counter_argument: A neutral rail and buttons alone could be a themed kit.
premise.answer: The actual host catalog launches real PTY sessions; the file explorer preserves machine scope and launches a terminal at the directory. Review must exercise these operations, not only inspect the shell.

stack.rationale: Preserves verified backend contracts and existing operations; Material-like spacing does not require a framework migration.
stack.alternative: MUI React components with a neutral theme, at the cost of a broad component migration.

rules.relationship: A developer must see the task and its available action before optional controls.
rules.rule: A 184px desktop navigation rail, compact header, and one scrollable task region; advanced launch controls are a disclosure.

check.how: Open Machines at desktop, short laptop, tablet, and phone sizes and launch a terminal.

rules.relationship: The user rejects blue accents, gradients, and pills but wants familiar controls.
rules.rule: Neutral paper/graphite surfaces, 4px control corners, 40–44px controls, 8px spacing increments, sans task text, ASCII chrome identity.

check.how: Inspect both themes and measure computed color and shape roles.

rules.relationship: Machine context identifies the execution and edit destination.
rules.rule: Machine selector above discovery and in file toolbar; selecting a new machine clears the explorer and editor.

check.how: Browse a test path, open the editor, and verify explicit terminal controls and selected machine.

approval.source: User explicitly authorized UI improvements during implementation and supplied the final Material/neutral/ASCII direction. This records implementation authorization, not approval of unseen screenshots.
approval.scope: Reversible implementation under the user-provided visual direction; developer instruction requires completing reviewable local work without an approval pause.

evidence: Opened eight /tmp/rain-ui-review screenshots; desktop rail and phone bottom navigation preserve one scrollable task region. Local HTTP terminal launch/stop passed.
Browser sent /help to a real echo session through the chat composer and opened desktop/phone populated chat captures.
Both themes opened; computed backgrounds/text are neutral RGB triples. Detector returned []. No overflow at 320,390,768,1280,1440 widths.
Browser entered /tmp/rain-http-check in the path form and opened a Unicode-named test file in the editor. HTTP read/write roundtrip passed.

findings.evidence: Independent reviewer identified default low-contrast placeholder. Opaque --text-muted applied, desktop and phone recaptured and reviewed.
findings.retest: Refreshed desktop-dark and phone-dark screenshots opened; reviewer scored placeholder resolved.

findings.evidence: Removed inline outline suppression and added focus-visible. Browser measured active TEXTAREA, focusVisible true, outline rgb(32,32,32) solid 2px; updated /tmp/rain-ui-review/editor-focus.png opened.
findings.retest: Keyboard Tab modality, active TEXTAREA, focusVisible true, computed 2px ink outline; editor-focus.png opened and confirmed.

limits: Physical phone and Android package are not tested in this design pass.
Remote SSH hosts require account configuration; the rendered review uses the local host.
